_comment: BRO-2943 (2026-09-08, owner-approved Option A): scrapingdogDailyCredits raised 45000 -> 100000 = the prepaid 3M-credit pack over a 30-day cycle. The old line matched the hardcoded breaker ceiling that tripped most days and rerouted traffic to ScrapingBee/Bright Data; the breaker is now plan-derived (~130-160K/day) so a 45K alarm fired on every normal day and carried no signal. Daily ALERT thresholds for check-provider-spend.js — owner-approved 2026-07-30 (Scraping Cost System v2, Option A). These are alarm lines, NOT enforcement: enforcement stays in the env-var caps (BROWSERBASE_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_DAY etc). Changing a number here changes when the digest yells, nothing else. BRO-2226 (2026-08-20): brightdataDailyUsd left AT 2.5 on purpose — investigated the 17/17-days-over alarm and found a real, fixable overspend (validate-show-venue.js's Tier-2 verifier was re-validating all ~40 provisional shows against Playbill on every single missing-show card attempt instead of just the added show, per data/audit/scraper-spend-ledger.jsonl the #1-2 BD caller every day; fixed to target --show=<addedId>), NOT a stale line — check-provider-spend.js's own decisionPrompt says raising this is an owner call, not a dispatched-session one, and the fix alone doesn't close the gap (BD volume is still several thousand req/day across many legitimate callers: opening-night-poller.js, audit-show-review-gap.js, gather-reviews.js). The alarm firing daily is correctly reporting real, uncapped overspend — leave it firing until either the owner raises the line or the other top callers get their own targeting fixes. Do not silently 3x this number to make the alarm stop.
_browserbaseDailyUsd_comment: BRO-3240 (2026-09-14): browserbaseDailyUsd's real basis changed — provider-spend-core.js used to price Browserbase per SESSION (BB_COST_PER_SESSION), which overstated cost ~10x and made this line fire on phantom spend nearly every day. It now prices real measured browser-minutes against Browserbase's actual Developer-plan rate (~$0.67/day amortized base + $0.12/browser-hour on measured usage, no monthly-quota gating — see provider-spend-core.js's BB_* constants for full sourcing). A normal day now costs ~$0.65-0.75; this $4 line means 'today's Browserbase spend is running well above the flat baseline' and is a real anomaly signal again, not a guaranteed-daily false alarm. Left at 4 — no finer-grained invoice data exists yet to justify a different number; revisit once a few weeks of the corrected model's real range are in the ledger.
_attributionCoverageMin_comment: S0-T7 (BRO-3008): owner-owned alarm line, NOT enforcement — below this, the digest adds a coverage warning naming BRO-2961 (the uninstrumented-direct-caller cleanup) instead of hiding the gap. 'coverage' here = what % of a provider's billed credits/units the printed top-N callers list itself accounts for (a high overall attributedPct can still hide a long tail the top-N list doesn't show).
_llmScoringRunUsd_comment: BRO-3381 (2026-09-15): alarm line for cumulative LLM scoring cost (Claude+OpenAI+Gemini) per GitHub Actions run id, summed across that run's index.ts invocations (main pass + drain). BRO-3392 (2026-09-15) instrumented comparative-rescore.ts with the same costUsd/runId recording, so its spend now sums into this same total too — see scripts/lib/llm-scoring-cost-recording.js and this run's data/llm-scoring-runs.json entries for the per-invocation breakdown. NOT enforcement — a --max-cost=10 scheduled default was reviewed and rejected the same day: --max-cost is inert in --batch mode (batch cost commits at submission, not per call, and scheduled non-chain runs use --batch), and the workflow's real spenders (batch pass, drain, comparative-rescore) are each a separate uncapped process, so a cap would enforce nothing on the runs it's meant for while a trip force-reds the job and the always() chain step still dispatches uncapped children. Measured basis: real successful runs on 2026-09-14/15 — scheduled run 34952979908 largest phase $1.0989, scheduled run 34831067835 largest phase $1.2126, small dispatch run 34987208122 $0.0251. Those are per-process, batch-discounted figures; chained sync runs price ~2x the batch rate, so a realistic busy day plausibly totals $4-6 across a run's processes — hence 6, not e.g. 8x one phase. Re-derive once real costUsd data accumulates in data/llm-scoring-runs.json.
